overall_verdict:
From the GPU and systems lens the five proposals collapse into three performance envelopes. On the web floor devices the task names (Mali-G5x/Xclipse Android in WebGL2, A12 iPad in Safari, desktop), A, B and D run the same policy against the same browser ceilings and differ only in how much machinery sits between the scheduler and the GL calls: A (direct WebGL2 from TypeScript, ~0.3 MB) has the least, D (Emscripten GLES3→WebGL2, ~1–1.6 MB) is a proven path, and B (wgpu's best-effort WebGL2 backend, 1.5–2 MB, open #4081/#3735/#10460) adds risk precisely on the devices that define the floor, mitigated only by its pre-planned exit to a raw WebGL2 draw path. C reaches the same pixels only after an 8–11 month replacement ladder on OpenSeadragon private API, with the MVP honestly 'MSK-class' rather than instant. E is a different physics: competitive on LAN, structurally behind tile prefetch on broadband, and a goal-1 failure on 4G with no client cache and no offline. Above the web ceiling, only B and D lift the iPad from ~40–50 ms/60 Hz to a documented 16.7–25 ms/120 Hz floor with native NEON decode and GB-class caches, and neither does so before month 18–20.

Four shared defects must be fixed in whatever is built, because every tile proposal inherited them from the corpus without checking the arithmetic: (1) the pinned base down to ≤4096 px is 70–85 tiles ≈ 70–85 MiB RGBA8, which is 55–66 % of the 128 MiB phone GPU budget and puts the design over budget at DPR 3 with two resident levels plus ring and prefetch; pin ≤2048² on GPU, hold 4096² as ASTC (16 MiB) or encoded-in-RAM, and restate the base as 2–5 MB of JPEG, not 1–2 MB; (2) at 2–4 MiB/frame a cold 20-tile level takes 5–10 frames (83–167 ms at 60 Hz) to reach the GPU on a phone with zero network latency, which is most of the Android TTS budget and must appear in the tables and gates; (3) the ≈2-vsync browser compositor floor and the per-tile ImageBitmap/texSubImage3D cost on iOS Safari and Mali-G52 Chrome are both unmeasured (my search found no Chrome Android touch-to-photon figure, and WebKit 234920/260460 remain open), so Stage 0 must ship a reference quad app and measure them before any latency promise is repeated; (4) the destination-level predictor 'from the first 1–2 pinch samples' is a hypothesis with a 34 % base rate of short bursts and no measured accuracy, so skipping intermediates must be gated on a confidence threshold and logged as waste. B's '≤256 layers × 512² (64 MiB each with mips)' is a 4× arithmetic error (256 MiB, 341 MiB with mips) that propagates into its phone budgets; D's AHardwareBuffer-into-texture-array zero-copy claim is not implementable on GLES 3.0 and will ship as the staging-copy fallback.

Recommendation: build A's web engine as the floor (direct WebGL2 in TypeScript, tested first on Xclipse/Mali-G52/A12, WebGPU as a measured enhancement) but write the scheduler, LOD, prefetch and cache policy as B's host-agnostic state machine with golden gesture replay, so it ports or compiles unchanged into a native shell; adopt C's server-first sequencing for months 0–3 (passthrough pyramid, manifest, edge translator, path-only cache keys), since it is identical across proposals and removes the only latency the public data proves avoidable; add D's native Metal iPad shell (CAMetalDisplayLink latency 1, shared-storage array textures, purgeable LRU tail, predicted touches to camera only) as the first post-v1 item, because it is the only route under the browser's 40–50 ms floor on the device pathologists actually hold; keep E as a later mode for 40-plex fluorescence, thin clients and SFU tumour boards, not as the viewer. The honest contract for radio links is the same in every tile proposal and should be stated as the product promise: never blank, ≤1 level soft during the gesture, sharp ≤700 ms p95, pre-downloaded coarse levels and client cache making zoom-out and revisits instant; no architecture makes a cold 4G tile sharp inside 100 ms.

scores.rationale: On the three named floor targets (Mali-G5x/Xclipse Android in WebGL2, A12 iPad in Safari, desktop) A has the fewest moving parts between the policy and the GPU: direct WebGL2 calls from a ~0.3 MB TS engine, texture arrays fed from vertex buffers (compat-mode safe), libjpeg-turbo WASM as reference with a self-certified createImageBitmap accelerator, and the L*∈[0.5,1.0] + pinned-ancestor + cross-level-blend policy from note 04 that actually addresses the four causes of blur. Its latency table is mostly honest about 4G (0.4–1.9 s cold transfer, 'bounded ≤1–2 levels soft, sharp ≤700 ms') but it over-sells the warm path: the row labelled '≈2 vsyncs' is quoted as 17–33 ms, giving a 25 ms lower bound that is one frame optimistic against B/C/D's 35–50 ms for the same browser pipeline, and the 2-vsync floor itself is [unverified] in the corpus (my search found no measured Chrome Android figure). The upload row hides the real floor-device constraint: at the stated 2–4 MiB/frame budget, a 20-tile destination level takes 5–10 frames (83–167 ms at 60 Hz) to reach the GPU even with zero network latency, which is already most of the 250 ms Android TTS target; A writes '3–6 frames'. The memory arithmetic does not close on phones: a pinned base down to ≤4096 px is 70–85 tiles (not 64) ≈ 70–85 MiB RGBA8, i.e. 55–66 % of the 128 MiB phone L0, and with two resident levels + ring + L*+1 prefetch at DPR 3 (~63 MiB) the design is over budget before any revisit caching; the base must be ASTC-compressed or kept off-GPU. Decode throughput on a 4-core A55 phone assumes 3 WASM workers get 3 cores, ignoring the browser's GPU/compositor/network threads, so 60–100 ms wall is optimistic (100–150 ms is more realistic). The destination-level predictor 'from the first wheel notch or pinch sample' is asserted without hedging; 34 % of bursts are <2.3 levels and skipping intermediates on a mis-prediction leaves nothing resident. What A cannot do is explicit and real: 60 Hz iPad, ~45 ms direct-touch input-to-photon against an 11 ms JND, no native GPU surface. Net: highest probability of shipping the floor contract soon, no path to the ceiling.
graft_ideas: Start-up self-certification of createImageBitmap against three golden tiles per browser build (colorSpaceConversion:'none', premultiplyAlpha:'none'); fall back to WASM libjpeg-turbo on any mismatch, always on Safari in Dx mode.
Author shaders once in WGSL and generate GLSL ES 3.00 at build time with naga-cli, golden-tested to ≤1 LSB against the WebGPU output (deck.gl discipline), instead of hand-maintaining two dialects.
Allocation-free core.tick(now, inputs) → {drawList, requests, evictions} driven from one rAF, with a CI gate of 'no main-thread task >8 ms during gestures'.
Service Worker explicitly off the hot path (50/250 ms cold start); OPFS via FileSystemSyncAccessHandle in a worker as the L2 encoded store, treated as refillable because ITP deletes it after 7 days.
Cellular 'moving tier': q75 4:2:0 for H&E only during gestures, refined to q90 4:4:4 on settle; IHC and cytology excluded; render DPR capped at 2 on metered links.
Capability token in the query string validated at the edge and stripped from a path-only cache key; no Authorization header so no CORS preflight per tile.
WebGL2 renderer first-class and tested first on Exynos/Xclipse, Mali-G52, Adreno 610 and Android 11; WebGPU feature-detected per capability, never per browser.

scores.rationale: B's policy is identical to A's and its measured evidence base (gap-2) is the strongest of the five: libjpeg-turbo bit-identical across native/wasm-SIMD/wasm-scalar, 0.98 MB gz renderer skeleton, 2.2× on 3 workers, worker messaging 0.15–0.3 ms/tile. The native shells are where B earns its zoom credit: CAMetalDisplayLink latency 1 on iPad gives a documented 2-interval floor (16.7 ms) versus the browser's ~40–50 ms, native NEON decode removes the 2–3× WASM penalty, and GB-class dynamic caches remove the phone memory squeeze; B's column A correctly uses the floor (17 ms) where D more honestly uses the typical 3 intervals. But the task's floor targets are web targets, and on exactly those devices B adds risk without adding capability: wgpu's WebGL2 backend is 'best-effort' by the project's own classification, #4081 (swapped texture-array layers on WebGL, open since 2023) hits B's GPU cache design directly, #3735/#10460 are open Safari failures with 2026 repros, and the 1.5–2.0 MB gz bundle costs 50–100 ms of compile plus 0.5–0.6 s of 4G download per cold page view. There is an outright arithmetic error in the renderer row: '≤256 layers × 512² Rgba8UnormSrgb (64 MiB each with mips)' is wrong by 4×; 256 layers of 512² RGBA8 is 256 MiB (341 MiB with mips), so either the arrays are 48–64 layers or the phone budgets in the same table do not fit. B shares the pinned-base-on-GPU and upload-budget blind spots with A (70–85 MiB base against a 128 MiB phone L0; 5 frames of upload for a cold level). To its credit B hedges the prefetch constants as hypotheses and pre-plans the exit to a raw web-sys WebGL2 draw path (+3 PM) via wgpu v30's texture interop, which means the web floor ends up as A's renderer with a wasm scheduler if G3–G6 fail; that exit is what keeps the zoom score close to A's. The native shells do not arrive until month 18–20, so for the first 18 months B's delivered zoom quality is A's with more weight. The FFI/shell cost (three UI implementations, seven release channels, quarterly wgpu majors) is honestly stated and is the main reason effort and risk score low.
graft_ideas: Engine as a pure state machine: tick(now_ns, inputs, viewport) → FrameOut, on_bytes, on_decoded, set_budget; the core owns no threads, DOM or sockets, so the same scheduler runs on a worker pool (web) and a rayon pool (native).

Golden gesture replay: a recorded pinch/wheel burst replayed through tick() must yield a byte-identical request sequence on every platform; this is the operational test of 'one zoom behaviour everywhere'.
One decoder codebase (libjpeg-turbo C, compiled natively via turbojpeg and to wasm via Emscripten -msimd128, no pthreads); Rust decoders rejected because measured non-identical (10–38 % of pixels).

Stage-0 go/no-go gates G1–G10 with numeric pass criteria on named floor devices (Mali-G52, Adreno 610, Xclipse, iPhone 12, 2020 iPad), especially G4 (texture-array correctness for every layer count 1…256) and G5 (≤2 ms per 512² upload, no main-thread stall >8 ms).
PresentSink and TileTextureStore traits isolating the present path and texture allocator so direct Metal (shared storage, purgeable LRU tail) can replace wgpu's path without touching the scheduler.
Dynamic memory budgets from OS signals (os_proc_available_memory, ActivityManager.MemoryInfo + onTrimMemory) rather than a static table; isLowRamDevice is false on every 3–4 GB phone.
Safari policy: WebGL2 default, WebGPU allow-listed per Safari major after a soak test, 'Restart with WebGL2' affordance (rerun precedent).
Per-tile provenance flag (passthrough vs re-encoded) carried from ingest into telemetry and Dx-mode records.

scores.rationale: C is right that the largest avoidable latency in deployed systems is server-side (MSK's +130 ms/FOV for transcoding) and its months 0–6 (pre-tiled passthrough, manifest, stateless edge translator, path-only cache keys) are work every other proposal also needs; that part is low-risk and correct. The client story is where the performance lens bites: the MVP is OpenSeadragon with re-tuned knobs, and C's own latency table concedes 6–12 ms/frame of OSD scheduler time on the floor Android (a third to two thirds of a 60 Hz frame before drawing), per-tile texImage2D with no upload budget (so every arriving tile burst stalls the main thread, WebKit 234920/260460 class), a 2D-canvas drawImage composite per frame, no mipmaps and no cross-level blend. C labels the MVP 'accepted-good (MSK-class)' rather than instant, which is honest, but it means goal 1 is not met until R1–R3 land in months 8–11, and R2 (the scheduler, i.e. the prefetch that makes residency ≥95 %) lives on OSD private API (TiledImage._updateLevel) that changed in both 6.0 and 6.1. After R1–R4 the pixels are produced by C's own texture-array drawer, shaders and WASM decoder, so pixel quality can match A, but the frame still carries an unmeasured 0.5–2 ms (MVP table says 2–4 ms post-R2 on Android) of OSD World/TiledImage bookkeeping per frame, which matters at 120 Hz desktop and on A55-class phones. The replacement-ladder triggers are a genuinely good discipline (named metric, named floor device), but the ladder's end state is A's engine plus an OSD compatibility shim and a 6–11 month delay on the zoom quality that is the number-one goal. C shares the pinned-base and upload-budget arithmetic gaps and adds a fluorescence MVP that re-fetches the viewport on every LUT change (300–800 ms). Reach is webview-only with no native viewport before post-v1. Effort (62 PM) and cost are the best of the five, which is exactly the trade C makes.
graft_ideas: Server-first sequencing for months 0–3 regardless of client choice: lossless passthrough via wsidicomizer/opentile, --add-missing-levels to complete the dyadic pyramid, ≤100 KB immutable per-slide manifest mapping (level,x,y) → (object, offset, length), two-pass ingest (≤4096 px levels first so the slide opens in seconds).

Replacement triggers written as named metrics on named floor devices (Siemens-star aliasing at s<0.75, pop-in count after settle, main-thread task >8 ms when ≥4 tiles land, drawImage composite >2 ms at 4K) rather than opinions.
Quality record (level wanted vs drawn per tile per frame) logged from M0 so NTF%, BAT and TTS exist before any renderer work.
OSD TileSource / DrawerBase contract and the IIIF/DZI/Annotorious ecosystem kept as a compatibility surface (adapter), not as the engine.
DICOMweb frames/{list} multipart retrieval as the standards-native coalescing path for DICOM sources; Zarr shards served as-is with CORS-safelisted Range (no preflight).
IIIF off-grid regions routed to a rate-limited libvips slow path; own clients always request grid-aligned tiles.

OSD default-knob audit as a checklist of anti-patterns to avoid in any engine: maxTilesPerFrame:1, immediateRender:false, blendTime:0, 1.2 s spring, ±1 quantised wheel with 50 ms throttle, CSS-pixel rendering.

scores.rationale: D has the most rigorous latency table of the five: it uses the typical native present path (3 intervals iPad, 4 Android) rather than the floor, separates cold-tail (1–3 tiles missing, TTS 22–68 ms p50) from whole-level-cold (215–800 ms), includes the web build 'for honesty', and states that nothing puts a direct-touch pinch under the 11 ms JND. The native levers it names are real and verified in gap-4: CAMetalDisplayLink preferredFrameLatency=1 with two drawables, storageModeShared 2D-array textures written with replace(region:slice:) from decode threads (true zero-GPU-copy on unified memory), volatile purgeable LRU tail that stops counting toward jetsam, postVsyncCallback preferred timeline and requestUnbufferedDispatch on Android, predicted touches feeding the camera only. One claim is overstated: an AHardwareBuffer cannot be bound as a layer of a GLES 2D-array texture, so 'decode into an AHardwareBuffer and bind via EGLImage' either forces per-tile textures (breaking the one-instanced-draw-per-level design on GLES 3.0, which has no bindless) or needs a GPU blit into the array, so Android upload is a cheap copy, not zero-copy; D's own fallback (glTexSubImage3D from staging) is what will actually ship. The web build is Emscripten GLES3→WebGL2, a decade-proven path (Unity/Godot) with lower abstraction risk than wgpu's WebGL backend and a smaller bundle (1.0–1.6 MB gz estimate) than B, so on the three named floor targets D's web path is roughly A's with a wasm scheduler and ~50–100 ms more cold start; it shares A's pinned-base, upload-budget and destination-predictor gaps. The Android native shell (where the mid-range-phone ceiling would be lifted) does not exist until month 20, and when it does D owns every Adreno/Mali/PowerVR/Xclipse driver bug itself (MapLibre's 2026 changelog is the cost evidence D cites against itself). Memory safety in C++ parsers of untrusted slide bytes is procedural (sandbox + fuzz + sanitizers ≈1 FTE recurring), five shells cost ~36 PM plus a 2–2.5× per-feature tax, and Metal+Vulkan+driver-debugging C++ engineers are the scarcest hire in the field; those drive the low effort, risk and maintainability scores despite the best native ceiling.
graft_ideas: Ship a reference quad app (raw Metal; raw Vulkan + SurfaceView; and a trivial WebGL canvas) inside the Stage-0 harness and write every latency gate as 'p95 ≤ reference-quad p95 + 1 interval' on the same device and firmware, because the browser 2-vsync floor and the native 2–4 interval floors are models, not measurements.

iPad present recipe: CAMetalDisplayLink preferredFrameLatency=1, maximumDrawableCount=2, presentsWithTransaction=false, framebufferOnly=true, overlays drawn in the same Metal frame; request CAFrameRateRange(80,120,120) only during gesture/inertia.

Shared-storage 2D-array tile textures with allowGPUOptimizedContents=false written from decode threads into fenced slots (MTLSharedEvent); LRU tail set volatile via setPurgeableState so it stops counting toward the jetsam footprint.
Predicted input (predictedTouches, MotionEventPredictor) feeds the camera target only, never tile requests.

Frame-budget partition 60/25/15 (pixels/overlays/UI) with overlays degraded first; vector tiles cut on the pixel pyramid grid with per-level representation switching (centroids → simplified → full polygons).

Fuzz target per reader before merge, 24 h zero-crash fuzz before any reader ships, ASan/UBSan/MSan CI, differential tests against tifffile/wsidicom/OpenSlide; applies to Rust parsers too (logic bugs, not just memory).
Qt QQuickItem desktop shell doubling as the Qt host SDK for napari/3D Slicer/vendor PACS clients; C ABI as the only frozen surface with Swift/Kotlin/Python/.NET regenerated from it.
Hardware JPEG decode explicitly ruled out as a lever on both platforms (Skia→jpeglib on Android, ImageIO undocumented on Apple); plan on libjpeg-turbo NEON thread pools.

scores.rationale: E solves the problems the other four spend their budget on (residency, decode CPU, phone VRAM, 40-plex compositing) by moving them to an L4 node, and on a hospital LAN its own model (pan 46/80 ms, zoom-step 48/85 ms p50/p95) is competitive with tile designs. Off LAN the physics is unfavourable and E says so: a sharp frame can never arrive before RTT + ~15 ms codec, video codecs have no scale predictor so every zoom frame is near-intra, and there is no client cache so each pan-back re-streams (pathologists pan back and forth constantly, Kayser 2009). On broadband the zoom-step sharp photon is 90/170 ms p50/p95 plus 130/300 ms more for the build-to-lossless still, versus tile prefetch that can have the destination level resident before burst end; on 4G it is 230/700+ ms plus a 0.7–2.4 s visible lossless build, a clear goal-1 failure. Several numbers are optimistic: the 250 KB scale-step frame is ~3× low (a 2400×1350 near-intra frame of tissue at E's own 0.23 B/px JPEG-q80 figure is ~745 KB, hence the 'drop to 720p' mitigation); the keyframe needed when the encoder restarts from 0 fps at rest is unbudgeted (hundreds of KB, ~0.8 s at 5 Mbps p95-low); and the client 'reprojection at the compositor floor' omits the per-vsync video→WebGL texture upload, which on iOS Safari is exactly the WebKit 234920/260460 stall class (25–36 ms per upload, still open), so the browser client is 1–2 frames worse than the table. With 1.25× overscan the transient stays ≤1.25× magnified only while zoom rate × round trip ≤ 0.3 levels, which holds on LAN/broadband at p50 and fails on 4G. Chroma is 4:2:0 whenever the image moves (DAB edges, chromatin), 4:4:4 only at rest; pixel determinism exists only for the still. Operationally it is a stateful 24×7 GPU fleet with warm pools, TURN for UDP-blocking hospitals, PHI in VRAM, data-residency-pinned GPUs, and 50–500× the per-session cost of tiles, with NVENC/nvJPEG single-vendor dependence; offline and air-gapped use are not supported at all. E's own §9.11 'verification debt' list (cloud-gaming figures from 2019, encoder throughput scaled from a 4090 by an assumed clock ratio, aggregator pricing) is accurate and disqualifying for the primary architecture, while its fit as a mode for thin clients, 40-plex fluorescence and SFU tumour boards is real.
graft_ideas: Separate 'navigation image' from 'diagnostic image' explicitly: a render-complete / build-to-lossless state at rest (PCoIP precedent) is the right framing for the Dx-mode 'rendering complete' flag in any architecture.

Client-side reprojection of the last complete frame with overscan: render the tile viewport into a 1.25× overscanned offscreen target and warp it when a frame would otherwise be late, so motion response never waits on tile arrival or upload.

Server-side GPU rendering as an optional mode selected per device/deployment: 40-plex fluorescence on 3 GB phones, headless still export, SFU fan-out of one render to a tumour board at zero marginal GPU cost.
Server pre-render/pre-fetch against the client's predicted pose at t + RTT + t_encode; the same One-Euro/Kalman extrapolation on both ends so a lost message does not stall.
Frame-id echo from server to client for end-to-end latency tracing, plus a photodiode rig from M0 because browsers hide decode/present timing.
nvJPEG/nvJPEG2000 on GPU for the Tier-D ingest path (J2K-SVS) where CPU decode-once is the bottleneck.
Phase-dependent encode policy (P-frames for pan, scale-stepped frames for zoom, 0 bps at rest) as a model for how a tile client should also vary its request policy by gesture phase.

overall_verdict: Weighted totals from this seat: B-rust-core 7.55, A-web-core 7.20, D-native-core 6.85, C-standards-incremental 6.15, E-server-render-stream 4.70. B wins the product and platform lens because it is the only proposal whose end state reaches every surface in goal 2 with high fidelity (web component, anywidget, Tauri desktop with a native GPU window, Swift/Kotlin GPU-surface SDKs, C ABI for Qt/C++/.NET/Java hosts, PyO3) while keeping one scheduler, one decoder (libjpeg-turbo, measured bit-identical) and one shader set to certify for a Dx edition; that single pathway plus a pen-first native iPad shell is what lets a viewer become the default across research and clinical settings, and note 07 shows native tablet viewing is the one market nobody serves. B's win is conditional: its web floor path is wgpu's best-effort WebGL2 backend with an open bug on the exact texture-array primitive the cache uses, so the Stage-0 gates G1–G10 and the pre-planned exit to a raw WebGL2 draw path must be binding, not aspirational; its 1.5–2.0 MB gz embed is a real integrator friction that must be answered with a dual-wasm build and a published embed-weight budget; and its iPad shell at month 18–20 is too late and should be pulled toward month 12 as D does. The final architecture should therefore be B's core and SDK surfaces with four grafts: A's web discipline (embed budget, Service Worker off the hot path, browser-decoder self-certification, WGSL-once with generated GLSL and ≤1 LSB goldens); C's entire server half (passthrough pre-tiled pyramids, two-pass ingest, DICOM WSI TILED_FULL plus OME-Zarr v0.5 as canonical stores, per-slide byte-range manifests, wsidicomizer/opentile/wsidicom as ingest backbone and CI oracles, OSD kept only as a perf-harness comparator and compatibility TileSource); D's native present-path recipe, purgeable/AHardwareBuffer upload paths, reference-quad gate and Qt QQuickItem shell-as-SDK, implemented as thin shells over the Rust C ABI rather than as a C++ core; and E as a later capability-selected mode for thin clients, 40-plex fluorescence, 3D and tumour-board fan-out, never as the viewer. Two cautions apply to every tile proposal and should be stated to the product owner now: no architecture makes a cold 4G viewport sharp inside 100 ms (the contract there is never-blank, ≤1-level transient, sharp within the inter-burst gap), and no web build lifts iPad Safari above WebKit's 60 fps preference, so 'instant on iPad' is a native-shell promise. Unverified items that could move these scores and should be closed in the spike: WebView2 WebGPU exposure, Tauri 2 mobile parity in 2026, wasm decode and compile cost on A55-class Android, and the Tauri native-surface-plus-webview layering B depends on for desktop.

scores.rationale: A is the most honest and most reach-efficient of the web-centric proposals: its LOD/hysteresis/trilinear-blend/pinned-base/destination-prediction policy is identical to B, C(v1) and D, and on the three contexts the goal names (low-end Android Chrome, iPad Safari, desktop) its probability of delivering is at least as high as B's, because gap-2's own decision table scores direct WebGL2 a 5 against wgpu-on-WebGL2's 4 on floor devices, the 0.3 MB TS bundle avoids a 50–100 ms wasm compile on 2020-class SoCs, and browser ANGLE has proven more robust than raw drivers on bad Android GPUs (wgpu #7669, https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/issues/7669). I still score zoom one point below B/D because A has no native shell at all: iPad stays at WebKit's 60 fps preference (verified at WebKit ToT in gap-3, `PreferPageRenderingUpdatesNear60FPSEnabled`) and ≈35–55 ms input-to-photon versus ≈20–25 ms native, and 3 GB Android never gets GB-class caches or threads. Refutations: the '~0.3 MB' figure excludes 60–90 KB per decoder module and the format clients; 'one team ships every platform in a year' is contradicted by its own v1 at 14–15 months; 'Full' fidelity for the Windows Tauri app rests on WebView2 exposing WebGPU, which the proposal marks unverified and which I also could not verify (GitHub access gated this session); Tauri 2 mobile parity is likewise unverified (the only official statement I found is the 2024 RC post saying mobile is 'not first-class yet', https://v2.tauri.app/blog/tauri-2-0-0-release-candidate/); and the two-dialect shader set with hand-patched generated GLSL is a permanent cost that the proposal under-weights. From a platform lead's seat the decisive weakness is spelled out in §9: no C ABI, no Swift/Kotlin GPU view, no Qt widget, so napari, 3D Slicer, QuPath and vendor PACS thick clients get a webview or nothing, which fails the 'native SDKs' clause of goal 2, and the iOS app carries App Store 4.2 risk and a ~15 % disk quota. Effort (49 PM MVP in ~6 months, 112 PM v1) and risk are the best of the engine-building proposals, and operating cost is near zero (R2/CDN, note 09 F8). Net: the right web engine discipline, the wrong end state for a product that wants to be the default viewer in research tools and on pen-first tablets.
graft_ideas: Per-browser-build start-up self-certification of createImageBitmap(blob,{colorSpaceConversion:'none',premultiplyAlpha:'none'}) against three golden tiles; browser decoder enabled only on pass, never on Safari in Dx mode; WASM libjpeg-turbo as the reference path everywhere.

Service Worker kept off the tile hot path (50/250 ms cold start desktop/mobile); OPFS FileSystemSyncAccessHandle worker as the L2 encoded-tile store, treated as a refillable cache because Safari ITP deletes it after 7 days regardless of persist().

A hard embed-weight budget as a product requirement: ≤300 KB gz core for third-party script-tag embeds, decoders as separate 60–90 KB modules, no COOP/COEP, prefix-scoped capability token in the query stripped from a path-only CDN cache key.
Cellular 'moving tier': DPR capped at 2, q75 4:2:0 for H&E only during motion refined to q90 4:4:4 at settle, IHC and cytology excluded (gap-1 F3 chroma risk); idle fan-out only on unmetered links.

WGSL authored once, GLSL ES 3.00 generated at build time with naga-cli and golden-tested against the WebGPU output at ≤1 LSB on SwiftShader/lavapipe plus real GPUs (deck.gl's dual-backend discipline).
Compatibility adapters as first-class deliverables: OpenSeadragon TileSource, OpenLayers Source and deck.gl layer wrappers so Slim/OHIF/Viv-ecosystem users can adopt incrementally.
Timing-Allow-Origin and Server-Timing headers on every tile response plus a per-frame quality record (level wanted vs drawn, deficit, TTS) exported from day one.
WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7/2.5.8 (single-pointer alternatives, 24 px targets) in the component from MVP.

scores.rationale: B is the only proposal whose end state covers every surface in goal 2 with high fidelity: web component and PWA, anywidget, Tauri desktop with a native wgpu window (which also resolves the Linux WebKitGTK no-WebGPU problem gap-3 settled), XCFramework via SwiftPM binaryTarget and AAR via UniFFI (the Mozilla pattern gap-4 verified), a cbindgen C ABI for Qt/C++/.NET/Java hosts, and PyO3 wheels, all driven by one JSON state document. Its zoom claim is the best evidenced in the set: libjpeg-turbo bit-identity across native/wasm-SIMD/wasm-scalar is measured (gap-2 §2.3), Rust decoders are correctly rejected on measured 10–38 % pixel differences, the wgpu renderer skeleton is 0.98 MB gz measured, and the Stage-0 gates G1–G10 with a pre-planned exit to a raw web-sys WebGL2 draw path via wgpu v30's `create_texture_from_webgl_handle` turn the main risk into a two-week experiment. Refutations: the web floor path is wgpu's 'Downlevel/Best Effort' WebGL2 backend, with #4081 (swapped layers in 2D texture arrays, open since 2023, https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/issues/4081) sitting on exactly the primitive the GPU cache is built from, and #3735 Safari tab kills with 2026 repros (https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/issues/3735); the 1.5–2.0 MB gz bundle is an estimate on top of a 0.98 MB measurement and the 50–100 ms low-end compile is an estimate, both real friction for third-party embeds; the Tauri 'native wgpu surface with TS chrome layered above' is flagged 'verify at Stage 2' and transparent webviews over native surfaces are historically fragile on Windows and macOS; and 'the same sequence of tile requests on every platform' is overstated, because request order after the first frame depends on byte-arrival timing, so the golden replay must record arrival times too or the claim shrinks to 'same first-frame requests and same draw list given the same residency'. The product cost is schedule: MVP at month 9 (≈80 PM), native iOS/Android shells and SDKs only at month 18–20 (≈160 PM), with the two graphics hires as a gating dependency; putting the iPad shell that late defers the one market note 07 found unserved (native pen-first tablet viewing). wgpu's roughly quarterly majors (28→30 in eight months) and the Rust+WGSL+Swift+Kotlin+TS hiring profile are the maintenance tax, offset by one scheduler, one decoder and one shader set to certify for a Dx edition. Operating cost is tile-serving cost, near zero. On balance B earns the top weighted score from this seat because reach, versatility and a single certifiable pixel pathway are what let a viewer become the default across research and clinical settings, provided the Stage-0 gates and the exit are treated as binding.
graft_ideas: The Engine contract as the architectural spine: tick(now_ns, inputs, viewport) -> FrameOut{draw_list, requests, cancels, uploads, quality}; on_bytes; on_decoded; set_budget; single-threaded, no DOM/OS access, host-supplied clock; recorded-gesture replay (with recorded byte-arrival times) as the cross-platform golden test.

Stage-0 spike gates G1–G10 with explicit pass thresholds on named floor devices (Mali-G52, Adreno 610, Xclipse, iPhone 12, 2020 iPad, Firefox Linux) and the pre-planned exit to raw web-sys WebGL2 sharing textures with wgpu.

libjpeg-turbo (C) as the only Dx-mode decoder on every platform, compiled natively via the turbojpeg crate and to wasm with -msimd128/no pthreads; one pinned OpenJPH build; reversible HTJ2K only in Dx until lossy identity is proven.
Safari policy, not feature test: WebGL2 default, WebGPU allow-listed per Safari major after soak (G6/G10), a 'Restart with WebGL2' affordance (rerun precedent), uncapturederror handling.

PresentSink and TileTextureStore traits isolating wgpu-hal escape hatches so shells can hand wgpu a preconfigured CAMetalLayer and shared-storage/purgeable tile textures without touching the scheduler.
Dynamic memory budgets from os_proc_available_memory / ActivityManager.MemoryInfo + onTrimMemory, never from isLowRamDevice; eviction before pressure; soak gates against jetsam.
stoi-model/stoi-source shared between client, edge and server so Zarr v3 shard geometry (512² chunks, 8×8 shards, 1 MiB-aligned ranges, index at end) agrees by construction.
Frame-budget partition 60/25/15 (pixels/overlays/UI) with overlays degraded first; vector tiles cut on the pixel pyramid grid keyed like raster tiles.

SDK packaging: XCFramework via SwiftPM binaryTarget with UniFFI Swift, Maven AAR via cargo-ndk + UniFFI Kotlin (JNA ≥5.12), cbindgen C ABI as the frozen surface, PyO3/maturin abi3 wheels, lockstep semver.

scores.rationale: C gets the sequencing argument right (server and network first; the only published deployed-viewer latency data, MSK's 108 vs 238 ms/FOV, blames transcoding and sparse pyramids, https://doi.org/10.5858/arpa.2021-0197-OA) and its standards story is the strongest at launch: DICOM WSI TILED_FULL with EOT plus OME-Zarr v0.5 as canonical stores, wsidicomizer/opentile/wsidicom (Apache-2, Sectra-funded, verified active) as the ingest backbone, and DICOMweb/IIIF/OME-Zarr as the only three client protocols. But the client thesis does not survive the corpus: note 03 scores adopting OpenSeadragon a 2 on instant-zoom ceiling ('fixable only by replacing the drawer'), note 07 calls blur-then-pop the norm for every OSD/OL viewer, and OSD's own maintainers describe the WebGL→2D-canvas composite as a design flaw (#2906, open, https://github.com/openseadragon/openseadragon/issues/2906; C verified today that 6.2 has no direct-WebGL mode). The replacement ladder's triggers (aliasing at s<0.75, pop-in >0 after settle, >8 ms main-thread tasks when ≥4 tiles land) are exactly the behaviours the corpus says OSD exhibits by construction, so they will fire immediately and the team ends up building A's engine anyway, later, inside OSD's World/TiledImage coordinate math with an unmeasured 0.5–2 ms/frame overhead and with R2 living on private `TiledImage._updateLevel` internals that changed in both 6.0 and 6.1 (C's own changelog verification). The MVP is explicitly 'MSK-class, not instant' on radio links, fluorescence is server-composited with a 300–800 ms viewport refetch per LUT change, and Dx-mode determinism does not exist before R3. Reach is A's platform matrix minus fidelity plus one genuine asset: OSD API and plugin compatibility (Annotorious, IIIF/DZI ecosystem) for research adopters; native SDKs are webview wrappers, so goal 2's native clause fails as in A. Effort is the best in the set (24 PM MVP, 62 PM v1), though 24 PM across 7–8 FTE in six months implies roughly half utilisation, so either the number or the team size is optimistic. Maintainability is weakened by dependence on a small volunteer core (14-month gap 5.0.1→6.0.0, 463 open issues) and a Ship-of-Theseus hybrid that is harder to reason about than either a clean adoption or a clean engine; two canonical stores double translator surface and push cost slightly above the other tile proposals. C is the proposal I would adopt for its server, ingest and standards half and reject for its client half.
graft_ideas: Server-first sequencing: fully pre-tiled, passthrough-encoded canonical pyramid with --add-missing-levels, no request-time transcoding, two-pass ingest (levels ≤4096 px plus manifest first so the slide opens in seconds).

DICOM WSI (TILED_FULL + Extended Offset Table, one instance per level, 512 px JPEG frames) as a canonical brightfield store alongside OME-Zarr v0.5, so DICOMweb claims are true at launch and the conformance statement is real; wsidicomizer/opentile/wsidicom as ingest backbone and byte-identity CI oracles.

Per-slide ≤100 KB immutable manifest mapping (level,x,y) or (c,z,level,x,y) to (object, offset, length) so the edge translator never parses DICOM or Zarr at request time; the Zarr shard index and DICOM EOT treated as the same idea.

Replacement triggers written as named metrics on named floor devices (Siemens-star fiducial at s<0.75 for aliasing; pop-in count after settle; main-thread task >8 ms when ≥4 tiles land; cache-hit-at-settle <90 %), with the quality record logged from M0 before any code is replaced.

An OSD-configured baseline (maxTilesPerFrame 100, imageLoaderLimit 24/64, immediateRender, blendTime 0.08, worker decode via downloadTileStart) kept in the perf harness as the public comparator the product is benchmarked against.
Label/overview/barcode withheld to a Tier-2 PHI bucket under a separate ACL that never reaches the CDN.
IIIF off-grid regions served through a rate-limited libvips slow path with a documented compliance level, while first-party clients only ever request grid-aligned tiles.
Design R1–R3 modules (drawer, scheduler, codecs) to run without OSD from day one so the compatibility shim, not the engine, is the disposable part.

scores.rationale: D is the proposal that most directly attacks the iPad and Android latency floors, and gap-4 backs it: the present-path levers it names (CAMetalDisplayLink with preferredFrameLatency 1, two drawables, presentsWithTransaction false, purgeable LRU-tail textures, AHardwareBuffer + EGLImage, postVsyncCallback preferred timelines, 120 Hz requested only during gestures) are all verified APIs that wgpu hides (no presentedTime, #9856; no AHB import), and D puts the SwiftUI iPad/macOS shell in the MVP at month 9 rather than B's month 18–20. The web path via Emscripten GLES3→WebGL2 is a decade-old production route and its honesty table (web build 43/70 ms vs native 30/43) is consistent with notes 04 and 11-gap-4. Refutations: 'small enough to write three times well' is contradicted by the proposal's own evidence that MapLibre is still adding Adreno 600 VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST workarounds in 2026, and gap-4's tradespace scores owning Vulkan/GLES/Metal backends a 1 on driver burden against wgpu's 5; parsing attacker-controlled TIFF/DICOM/Zarr/iSyntax bytes in C++ makes memory safety procedural (~1 FTE of fuzzing/sanitizers forever) precisely when §524B and the CRA are tightening hospital security review; Djinni's Snap fork recency is low-confidence in the proposal and I could not verify it either (GitHub gated), leaving hand-written JNI as the realistic Kotlin path; Qt on Windows carries LGPL-3 dynamic-linking terms and a look that LIS procurement may reject (the proposal budgets a +4 PM WinUI alternative); and five shells cost 36 PM plus a 2–2.5× per-feature tax, with the Linux shell explicitly trailing. Reach is as broad as B's, with the Qt QQuickItem doubling as the SDK for napari/3D Slicer hosts a genuine plus, but the web embed is 1.0–1.6 MB gz (estimate) and 'second-class in ceiling' by its own admission. Effort (68 PM MVP, 130–200 PM v1 at month 20 across six compilers and seven channels) and risk (five-shell drift rated High/High by the authors) are the worst among the tile proposals, and hiring C++ engineers with both Metal and Vulkan depth is the scarcest profile in the set. Maintainability suffers from CMake/vcpkg across Xcode/NDK/MSVC/Emscripten, the perpetual driver-bug burden and the UX fragmentation of SwiftUI + Compose + Qt + Lit, although the C ABI is the most durable SDK surface of any proposal. D is B's twin with better present-path control and worse everything-else; its native recipes belong in the final design, its language and shell count do not.
graft_ideas: The native present-path recipe: CAMetalDisplayLink preferredFrameLatency 1, maximumDrawableCount 2, presentsWithTransaction false with overlays drawn in the same Metal frame, CAFrameRateRange(80,120,120) only during gesture/inertia; Android SurfaceView + postVsyncCallback preferred timeline + two-image swapchain + setFrameRate(120, ONLY_IF_SEAMLESS) + requestUnbufferedDispatch.
Input prediction (predictedTouches, MotionEventPredictor) feeds the camera target only, never tile requests; hover/pointer-down prefetch of L*+1 buys 100–300 ms before motion.

iOS LRU-tail tile textures set volatile so they stop counting toward the jetsam footprint; Android decode into AHardwareBuffer bound via EGLImage for zero-copy upload (requires a wgpu-hal patch if wgpu is kept).

Reference quad apps (raw Metal; raw Vulkan + SurfaceView) shipped inside the Stage-0 harness, with the viewer gate defined as p95 input-to-photon ≤ reference-quad p95 + 1 interval on the same device and firmware.
Qt QQuickItem as a thin shell over the core's C ABI so the Linux/Windows desktop and the Qt host SDK (napari, 3D Slicer, vendor C++ clients) are the same artefact.

Reader hardening as release policy: libFuzzer + ASan/UBSan/MSan CI, structure-aware generators, 24 h fuzz with zero crashes before any reader ships, differential tests against tifffile/wsidicom/OpenSlide, SBOM in every release (applies to Rust parsers for logic bugs too).
Shells capped at 3–5 kLOC with every tool/annotation/panel/channel state machine implemented as a core view-model over the C ABI; a shared web view for non-viewport chrome inside native shells.
Caddy (or nginx-quic) for TLS and HTTP/3 termination in front of the tile service instead of writing QUIC; libcurl with ngtcp2/nghttp3 in native shells; libdicom (C, MIT) for local DICOM WSI reading.

scores.rationale: E is the most self-critical proposal and the one the corpus had already adjudicated: note 05 F10 concludes pixel streaming is 'a mode, not the architecture', because the mechanism every other note identifies for instant zoom, client residency, is structurally unavailable to it. Its own latency table concedes the goal is missed off-LAN: sharp photons after a zoom step arrive at 90/170 ms p50/p95 on broadband and 230/700+ ms on 4G, the lossless still that is the only 'diagnostic' state takes +130/300 ms on broadband and +0.7/2.4 s on 4G, zoom is the codec's worst case (each scale-step frame re-sends the whole viewport, so tiles need about half the bytes), and revisits, which Kayser 2009 shows dominate pathologist navigation, re-stream through the full round trip every time. The pan-motion claim (client reprojection within the compositor floor) is sound and the 1.25× overscan is a clever bound, but 'no blurry tiles during or after zoom' is violated by design for one RTT plus codec beyond that margin. Verification is weak where it matters: the proposal's §9.11 admits the latency model is cross-checked against 2019 cloud-gaming measurements and 'low-quality 2026 reports', the L4 session count scales RTX 4090 encoder figures by an assumed clock ratio, and Safari WebRTC AV1/VP9 and Apple 4:4:4 HEVC decode are unconfirmed; the one figure I could verify is the g2-standard-4 price at $0.7068/h (https://cloud.google.com/products/compute/pricing/accelerator-optimized, https://calculator.holori.com/gcp/vm/g2-standard-4), which supports its own 50–500× per-session cost multiple versus tiles. From a platform seat the reach story inverts: the 60–120 KB client is the smallest embed, but it needs egress to a regional GPU edge, UDP or a TURN relay that hospital networks often block, a stateful warm-pool GPU fleet pinned to each data-residency zone, offers no offline or air-gapped use at all, and is not a DICOMweb/IIIF/OME-Zarr client, so IDC/Slim-style serverless viewing against a third-party archive is outside its model. Versatility is strong where the GPU is the point (40-plex fluorescence at channel-independent bandwidth, GPU AI overlays, server-side registration, SFU fan-out for tumour boards) and weak on interaction feel (window/level drags are round trips) and on pixel determinism (hardware video decoders are not bit-exact; Dx claims cover rest only). Effort to MVP is modest (31 PM) but v1 excludes offline and needs scarce WebRTC/QUIC transport engineers, and the operations profile (24×7 GPU fleet, PHI in VRAM, NVENC/nvJPEG under proprietary licences) is a different company from a CDN-fronted object store. E should be built later as a capability-selected mode on top of the winning tile core, not as the viewer.
graft_ideas: Pixel streaming as an optional, capability-selected mode (thin clients below the WebGL2 floor, 40-plex fluorescence, z-stack volume rendering, GPU AI overlays) where the server runs the same core scheduler/LOD policy against LAN latencies.

Build-to-lossless at rest: an explicit render-complete still (libjpeg-turbo/PNG, deterministic) as the only Dx-mode state, with the moving image labelled 'navigation'; the PCoIP precedent for regulatory framing.
Headless server rendering of stills for snapshots with scale bar, reports, teaching exports and a Python Session API returning numpy arrays, reusing the same renderer and policy as the client.
One render fanned out through an SFU for tumour boards and teaching: perfectly synchronised views at zero marginal GPU cost, follow-me cursors as overlay state.
Vector overlays (annotations, measurements, UI, scale bar) composited in slide coordinates above any lossy image surface, never rasterised into it.
Server-side frame ids echoed by the client plus a photodiode/high-speed-camera rig from M0 as the only credible end-to-end latency instrument, since browsers hide decode and present timing.
Scale-stepped frame cadence (emit a new frame when scale drifts ≥1.2× or 100 ms elapses, animate locally in between) as the codec policy for any future video mode.
GPU-accelerated lazy tiling (nvJPEG2000/cuCIM) for J2K-SVS and other Tier-D formats on the ingest side, where client determinism is not at stake.
Honest per-network SLO publication (LAN / broadband-edge / 4G, p50 and p95) as a product practice regardless of architecture.

overall_verdict: Weighted scores (zoom 0.35, reach 0.20, versatility 0.10, effort/risk/maintainability 0.10 each, cost 0.05): A 7.10, B 7.10, D 6.50, C 5.90, E 4.20. From the engineering-manager seat the panel should discard E (physics, cost and offline/UDP constraints rule it out as the primary architecture; keep it as a later thin-client/fluorescence/tumour-board mode) and D (the highest ceiling bought with the scarcest hires, three self-owned GPU backends whose driver bugs are ours — the option gap-4 explicitly rejected — a procedural rather than language memory-safety story for untrusted-slide parsers, and the slowest time to revenue). C is the right first six months of server and ingest work for any winner but the wrong client bet: its 62 pm is at least 30% under-estimated because R1-R4 rebuild everything A builds, and it ships OpenSeadragon's documented blur-then-sharp behaviour for roughly a year on a volunteer project's private API. A and B tie, and the tie-break is the dead-end question: A's documented ceiling (no native GPU surface, no C ABI, 60 Hz iPad for ever, a second engine if any native requirement arrives) is exactly the bet I am asked to avoid, while B's risks (wgpu-on-WebGL2 correctness, 1.5-2 MB bundle, Rust+Swift+Kotlin hiring, 18-20 month v1) each have a priced exit. I therefore rank B first by a narrow margin, with three conditions that are themselves grafts from the losers: (1) take gap-2's option C up front — Rust core state machine compiled to wasm, but a hand-written direct WebGL2 draw path on the web (wgpu v30 interop keeps textures shared; +3 pm) so the floor devices never depend on wgpu's best-effort backend and the web bundle shrinks toward A's; (2) sequence delivery like A and C — months 0-6 are the pre-tiled canonical store, manifest, edge and a lean TypeScript web shell, with native shells only after the web build has passed the M1/M2 gates on the floor devices; (3) adopt D's present-path and zero-copy recipes behind B's PresentSink/TileTextureStore traits and D's fuzz-first reader policy, and adopt E's regulatory framing (Dx = deterministic settled frame). Realistic planning numbers for that synthesis: ~55-65 pm to a web MVP at month 6-7, ~150-170 pm to a v1 with native iPad/Android at month 18-20, 9 FTE growing to 12-13, with the two graphics engineers and the performance/QA engineer hired first and a two-week Stage-0 spike (G1-G10) as the first funded milestone. Unverified items that would change this verdict if they fail: wgpu texture-array correctness on WebGL2 (#4081) and Safari stability (#3735/#10460) in the spike, and real WASM libjpeg-turbo decode cost on A55-class Android.

scores.rationale: The engine design is the corpus's own recommendation for web (note 03 option F: custom TS renderer, texture-array cache, trilinear + cross-level blend, zero-alloc loop, 6-9 pm) and every mechanism is traceable to a verified fact: WebGL2 at 97% reach as the floor, Xclipse WebGPU-blocklisted, compat-mode limits (4096^2 textures, 16 KiB UBO, whole-array views), no SAB so it embeds without COOP/COEP, WASM libjpeg-turbo bit-identical with createImageBitmap self-certified per browser (gap-2 measured 0 differing pixels). Its latency table is honest and matches the corpus floors (warm path = browser floor + 0; 4G 'bounded, not hidden'); I could not refute it, only note that the 10 kLOC and 49 pm MVP figures assume engineers who have shipped a GPU streaming renderer, which is also the scarcest hire for every proposal. The ceiling is stated plainly and I verified it is real: WebKit's PreferPageRenderingUpdatesNear60FPSEnabled defaults true, WKWebView cannot lift it without private SPI, so iPad is 60 Hz with ~35-55 ms input-to-photon forever under this architecture, and macOS desktop in WKWebView loses ProMotion. The two-dialect shader set (WGSL authored, GLSL ES generated by naga-cli then 'hand-patched') is a maintenance smell: generated-then-patched code is re-patched on every shader change, and two renderers must stay within 1 LSB. Reach is where it loses: goal 2 names native SDKs and the proposal says in §9 it 'fails it' if that means a GPU surface or C ABI; the mobile apps are WebKit/WebView wrappers with App Store 4.2 exposure, ~15% disk quota and no predicted touches. The strategic dead end is that any later native requirement (07 F7 says a pen-first native tablet viewer is the largest unserved gap) means a second engine, i.e. the classic web-first-then-rewrite trap. On effort, risk, hiring (TypeScript pool), licensing (all permissive, LGPL/GPL server-isolated) and operating cost (R2/CDN, a few hundred dollars a month per note 09 F8) it is the best-behaved proposal. Unverified items it depends on are minor and flagged by the author: WebView2 WebGPU (learn.microsoft.com unreachable from this sandbox) and Tauri 2 mobile parity (2024 official statement says production-ready with fewer plugins).
graft_ideas: Ship web first with a lean (~0.3 MB gz) TypeScript shell and a direct WebGL2 draw path on floor devices, with WebGPU as a measured enhancement, never a dependency.

Start-up self-certification of browser decoders: createImageBitmap(blob,{colorSpaceConversion:'none',premultiplyAlpha:'none'}) decodes three golden tiles and is enabled per browser build only if hash-identical to the WASM libjpeg-turbo reference; always WASM on Safari in Dx mode.
No-SharedArrayBuffer executor (clamp(hardwareConcurrency-1,1,3) workers, transferables only, 0.3-0.5 ms/tile) so the component drops into any page, iframe or Android WebView without COOP/COEP.

Service Worker kept off the tile hot path (50/250 ms cold start desktop/mobile); OPFS FileSystemSyncAccessHandle store in a worker, treated as a refillable cache because Safari ITP deletes it after 7 days regardless of persist().

Cellular policy: DPR capped at 2, H&E-only q75 4:2:0 'moving tier' refined to q90 4:4:4 on settle, IHC and cytology excluded; prefetch capped at 50% of measured bandwidth and 25% of request slots with ≤50% waste as Stage-1 acceptance.
Capability token in the query, validated at the edge and stripped from a path-only CDN cache key; HTTP/2 kept first-class because Samsung Internet has no HTTP/3.
Feature-detect per capability never per browser, weekly canaries on Chrome/Safari/Firefox betas, per-Safari-major WebGPU allow-list after soak (the rerun precedent).
Team shape: a dedicated performance/QA engineer owning the device lab and gates from M0, and a 0.5 FTE practising pathologist from day one.

scores.rationale: This is the corpus's recommended shape (note 06 option c, gap-2 decision 'B unless the spike fails G3-G6, then C') and the proposal adopts the gap notes' corrections faithfully: libjpeg-turbo C compiled natively and to wasm instead of Rust decoders (zune-jpeg differs in 37.6% of pixels, measured), single-threaded core on the web (wasm atomics still unstable at Rust 1.99), dynamic memory budgets, Safari defaulting to WebGL2. Its central promise, a recorded gesture replayed through tick() yielding an identical request sequence on every platform, is the only testable form of 'one zoom behaviour everywhere' and is a genuine architectural advantage over A/C for prefetch tuning and Dx-mode determinism. The web-floor risks are real and I could confirm each: wgpu's WebGL2 backend is 'Downlevel/Best Effort', the GPU tile cache is a 2D texture array and #4081 (swapped layers on WebGL) has been open since 2023, Safari tab kills (#3735) and black frames (#10460) are open, and the dual-backend bundle is 1.5-2.0 MB gz versus ~0.3 MB for A (gap-2 measured 0.98 MB for a renderer skeleton alone), which is 1.2-1.6 s on a 10 Mbit radio before the first tile and a hard sell for third-party embeds. The mitigation is credible because the exit is cheap: wgpu v30's create_texture_from_webgl_handle makes a raw web-sys WebGL2 draw path a +3 pm addition, and gap-2's own decision table actually scored that variant (option C) 82 to B's 78; I would adopt it up front rather than wait for the spike to fail. The Tauri desktop claim (native wgpu surface with TS chrome layered above) is marked 'verify at Stage 2'; I verified today that WRY ships examples/wgpu.rs combining a wgpu surface and a WebViewBuilder in one window, so the pattern exists, but transparent overlay and hit-testing across WebView2/WKWebView/WebKitGTK remain unverified and the fallback (wasm inside the webview) loses the 120 Hz desktop win. Effort is the honest price: 80 pm to a month-9 MVP and ~160 pm to v1 at month 18-20, native mobile arriving last, Rust+WGSL+Swift+Kotlin+TS in one team with graphics seniors hired first, seven release channels in lockstep and wgpu majors roughly quarterly (28→30 in eight months, vendored and pinned). UI is written three to four times and the proposal says so; the Dropbox shared-C++ retreat is the right cautionary tale and 'share the engine, not the UI' plus UniFFI is the right answer. Licensing is clean (Apache-2.0, permissive-only client core, MPL tooling does not encumber generated bindings) and memory safety by language is a materially better story than D's under §524B and the CRA. Operating cost is identical to A/C/D (stateless edge, zero-egress storage).
graft_ideas: The Engine contract: a pure single-threaded state machine `tick(now_ns, inputs, viewport) -> FrameOut{draw_list, requests, cancels, uploads, quality}` plus `on_bytes`, `on_decoded`, `set_budget`, with a host-supplied clock and no threads, DOM or OS access; recorded-gesture replay as a CI golden asserting identical request sequences on every platform.
Client and server share the pyramid-model and source crates so shard geometry (512² chunks, 8×8 shards, 1 MiB-aligned ranges, index at end) agrees by construction.

Two small traits (`PresentSink`, `TileTextureStore`) isolating the wgpu-hal escape hatches so a shell-created CAMetalLayer, shared/purgeable textures or a direct-Metal present path can be swapped in without touching the scheduler.
Vendor and pin wgpu per release train with a two-week upgrade window gated on texture-array correctness and WebGPU-vs-WebGL2 golden images (≤1 LSB).

Stage-0 spike with explicit go/no-go gates (bundle ≤2.0 MB gz, cold start ≤300/150 ms, p99 ≤16.7 ms on Mali-G52/Adreno 610/Xclipse/iPad, 1..256-layer array correctness, Safari 500-reload soak, 1,000/1,000 decoder hash identity) and a pre-planned exit to a raw WebGL2 draw path.
Dynamic memory budgets from os_proc_available_memory / ActivityManager.MemoryInfo + onTrimMemory with the LRU tail marked volatile; never a static per-device table.
Dual-wasm delivery (WebGPU-only module at 0.21 MB gz for capable browsers, full module otherwise) if embed customers object to bundle weight.
FFI discipline: batch input samples into one tick per frame, keep draw lists and uploads inside the core, design per-tile or per-feature callbacks as bulk buffers.

scores.rationale: The server-first thesis is the best-evidenced claim in any proposal: MSK's deployed data shows request-time transcoding costs ~130 ms per field of view (108 ms native blocks vs 238 ms transcoded) and note 05 agrees that residency and hit rate dominate before the renderer does, so months 0-6 spent on a fully pre-tiled canonical pyramid, a ≤100 KB tile→byte-range manifest and a stateless edge is work every other proposal also needs and C does it first and cheapest. The client thesis is weaker than it looks. The author verified the OSD seams from source, but the corpus's own survey (note 03 §2.2/2.9) scores OSD 2/5 for instant-zoom ceiling because its WebGL drawer uses one texture per tile with no generateMipmap, a two-pass 2D-canvas drawImage composite and main-thread uploads, and the proposal concedes the Android floor device will trigger R1 'almost certainly'; so for roughly the first year the product ships the blur-then-sharp behaviour goal 1 forbids, and zoom-intent prefetch (R2) does not arrive until months 8-11. R2 sits on private API (`TiledImage._updateLevel`, `_compareTiles`) that changed in 6.0 and 6.1; I checked the npm registry today: 5.0.1 shipped 2024-12-09, then nothing until 6.0.0 on 2026-02-18, then 6.0.1, 6.0.2, 6.1.0 (2026-08-06) and 6.1.1 (2026-09-09), i.e. a small volunteer project with bursty cadence, healthier this year but still a liability to pin a clinical product's scheduler to. The effort figure does not survive scrutiny: by v1 the drawer, scheduler, decoder and gesture router are all rewritten (R1-R4), which is essentially A's engine, yet the client line is 21 pm against A's ~40-49 pm for the same functionality; I would plan on 80-90 pm to v1, still the cheapest, but not 62. MVP fluorescence is server-composited with a 300-800 ms viewport refetch per window/LUT change, and two canonical stores (DICOM WSI and OME-Zarr) double translator and ingest surface. Reach is the web ceiling plus webview wrappers with 'functional parity, not native latency', and a later native viewport would reuse only R2/R3 unless they are written in Rust→WASM up front, which the proposal itself recommends (+1-2 pm) while admitting it reintroduces the risk the angle avoids. Licensing is clean (OSD BSD-3, wsidicomizer/opentile Apache-2.0 with Sectra behind them, LGPL/GPL isolated), operating cost is the same near-zero as A/B/D, and the proposal's §9.10 is the most honest sentence in the set: if launch customers are tablet- or cellular-first, this sequencing is wrong.
graft_ideas: Server and network first: a fully pre-tiled canonical pyramid with no request-time transcoding, two-pass ingest (levels ≤4096 px plus manifest in seconds, base levels streamed in the background) and a per-slide ≤100 KB immutable manifest mapping (level,x,y) to (object, offset, length) so the edge never parses DICOM or Zarr at request time.

Replacement-ladder discipline for any adopted component: each swap is triggered by a named metric on a named floor device (3 GB Mali-G52 Android, A12 iPad, Intel-iGPU laptop) measured by the quality record, not by preference.

A day-one OpenSeadragon configuration profile (maxTilesPerFrame 100, imageLoaderLimit 24/64, immediateRender, blendTime 0.08, animationTime 0.12, DPR-aware minPixelRatio, worker decode via downloadTileStart) kept as the public benchmark baseline and as the OSD TileSource/Annotorious compatibility shim.

wsidicomizer/opentile/tifffile as lossless passthrough tier and CI byte-identity oracles; DICOM WSI TILED_FULL with Extended Offset Table, one instance per level, LABEL/OVERVIEW withheld to a separate PHI-tier bucket.
A single 'base bundle' object (levels ≤4096 px) preloaded at case open plus preconnect and 103 Early Hints to the tile host, so zoom-out and the first zoom-in never miss.

Only three tile protocols spoken by the client (DICOMweb frames incl. framelist, Zarr v3 shard ranges with CORS-safelisted Range, IIIF Image 3.0 grid-aligned fast path) with a published DICOM conformance statement at launch.
Honest external claims until measured: 'validated for diagnosis on tablets, unproven for speed', and MVP radio-link performance described as MSK-class rather than instant.

scores.rationale: D has the highest latency ceiling of the five because it alone reaches every lever gap-4 says matters on the devices that define the floor: CAMetalDisplayLink with preferredFrameLatency 1 and two drawables, storageModeShared texture arrays written with replace(region:slice:) from decode threads, purgeable LRU tails, AHardwareBuffer import via EGLImage, postVsyncCallback preferred timelines and predicted input feeding only the camera target; its latency table (iPad floor 2 intervals, typical 3; Android 3/4) reproduces the gap-4 model exactly and it correctly refuses the 'hardware JPEG decode' lever that gap-4 found does not exist. The web build via Emscripten GLES3→WebGL2 is the Unity/Godot path and I accept it as proven, with the same 60 Hz Safari and single-threaded ceilings as everyone else and a 1.0-1.6 MB gz download. The problem is the price of owning the stack. gap-4 §2.10 evaluated exactly this option ('direct Metal + direct Vulkan + GLES fallback written by us') and rejected it with MapLibre's 2026 changelog as the cost evidence (Adreno 600 VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST workarounds still being extended, Adreno 3xx invisible raster layers); D mitigates by making GLES the Android default and Vulkan allow-listed, which is sensible, but every Adreno/Mali/PowerVR/Xclipse quirk in three hand-written backends is then D's bug to find, where B inherits Firefox's wgpu workarounds for free. 'Three backends in ~6 kLOC' is optimistic: a Vulkan backend with swapchain recreation, VMA, synchronisation and device-loss recovery alone is typically that size. C++ parsing of attacker-controlled TIFF/DICOM/Zarr/iSyntax bytes is a procedural rather than language guarantee (OpenSlide shipped two memory-safety CVEs in 4.0.1 this year) and the proposal budgets ~1 FTE of sandboxing, sanitizers and fuzzing indefinitely, which under §524B and the CRA is a weaker story than Rust by construction. Five shells (SwiftUI iPad, SwiftUI macOS, Compose, Qt 6, Lit) are quantified at ~36 pm and a permanent 2-2.5× feature tax, with the Dropbox failure mode named; Qt brings LGPL-3 dynamic-linking terms and a procurement risk the proposal budgets +4 pm (WinUI) to escape. Hiring is the scarcest of any proposal: C++ engineers with Metal and Vulkan and driver-debugging depth; the build is CMake+vcpkg across Xcode, NDK, MSVC and Emscripten (+3 pm admitted); the Snap Djinni fork's recency is low confidence (I could not reach github.com from this sandbox either) and D keeps a hand-written JNI fallback. 68 pm MVP at month 9 (with iPad shell) and 130-200 pm to v1 at month 20 is the slowest time to revenue, and the proposal says so. Operating cost and licensing of the server side are as clean as A/B/C.
graft_ideas: The native present-path recipe: CAMetalDisplayLink with preferredFrameLatency=1, maximumDrawableCount=2, presentsWithTransaction=false, framebufferOnly, overlays drawn in the same Metal frame, CAFrameRateRange(80,120,120) requested only during gesture/inertia; Android SurfaceView + postVsyncCallback preferred timeline + setFrameRate(120, ONLY_IF_SEAMLESS) + requestUnbufferedDispatch + two-image swapchain; predictedTouches/MotionEventPredictor feed the camera target only, never tile requests.

Zero-copy upload: storageModeShared 2D-array textures with allowGPUOptimizedContents=false written via replace(region:slice:) from decode threads into fenced slots (MTLSharedEvent); decode into AHardwareBuffer bound through EGLImage on Android; purgeable/volatile LRU tail so it stops counting toward jetsam.
Ship reference quad apps (raw Metal; raw Vulkan+SurfaceView) inside the Stage-0 harness and gate on 'p95 input-to-photon ≤ reference-quad p95 + 1 interval' measured with a photodiode rig.

Fuzz-first readers: no reader merges without a libFuzzer/ASan target, 24 h zero-crash run, structure-aware generators and differential tests against tifffile/wsidicom/OpenSlide; parse untrusted slide bytes sandboxed (wasm on web, separate process on desktop).

Shells are surfaces only: every state machine (tools, annotation editing, layer panel, channel settings) is a core view-model exposed through the ABI, shells capped at 3-5 kLOC, non-viewport chrome allowed to be a shared web view.

A device allow/deny list in the core (vendor/renderer string → backend preference) with GLES as the Android default, Vulkan behind an allow-list and automatic GLES retry on VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST in the first N frames.
Shell cost as a planning constant: ~36 pm for five shells and a 2-2.5× per-feature tax relative to a single web UI.
If Qt hosts (napari, 3D Slicer, vendor PACS) are a confirmed target, the Qt QQuickItem is the Qt SDK rather than a separate deliverable; Panama FFM/P-Invoke on the frozen C ABI for Java/.NET hosts.

scores.rationale: E is the most candid proposal and the least suitable for the stated goals. Its own latency table shows where it fails: sharpness after a zoom step is RTT plus codec, 48/85 ms on LAN, 90/170 ms on broadband and 230/700+ ms on 4G, and the lossless still at rest takes 0.3-2.4 s on 4G, which the author labels a goal violation; zoom-in is the worst case for inter-frame video coding (near-intra, ~2× the bytes of tiles for a 1→4× zoom), there is no client cache so every return pan re-streams through the full round trip, and the moving image is 4:2:0 chroma-subsampled on every mobile decoder, a specific hazard for DAB edges and HER2-low membranes that gap-1 flags. The corpus already evaluated this (note 05 F10) and concluded pixel streaming is a mode selected by device capability, not the architecture; E argues the contrary case well but does not overturn the physics. Where it wins is real: client-side reprojection puts motion at the platform floor with no network in the loop, rendering quality is uniform from a 2017 Android phone to a 4K workstation, fluorescence bandwidth is independent of channel count, GPU AI overlays are free, and on a hospital LAN with an on-prem L4 it is competitive with tiles at p50. Reach fails goal 2 on two counts the proposal states itself: no offline or air-gapped use without a second reduced viewer, and hospital networks that block UDP force TURN/TCP with head-of-line blocking; it is also not a zero-footprint DICOMweb/IIIF client, which IDC/Slim-style deployments expect. Operating cost is 50-500× tiles by the author's arithmetic ($0.06-0.35 per active hour plus 1.1-1.8 GB/h of egress, $250-900 per pathologist-year, GPUs pinned to every data-residency region, 60-120 s cold starts requiring warm pools) against a few hundred dollars a month for the tile architectures. Maintainability carries single-vendor proprietary dependencies (NVENC, nvJPEG under the CUDA EULA), a WebRTC/QUIC transport stack whose engineers are the scarce hire, GPL landmines carefully avoided (Sunshine/Moonlight, x264/x265) and a 24×7 stateful GPU fleet with PHI in VRAM. The effort estimate is internally inconsistent (78 pm to v1 against a stated 10-FTE team for 9-12 months, i.e. 90-120 pm) and §9.11 lists the verification debt plainly: the latency model is cross-checked against 2019 cloud-gaming figures and low-quality 2026 reports, L4 session counts are scaled from RTX 4090 encoder numbers by an assumed clock ratio, and GCP pricing is an aggregator's figure. Regulatory framing is the one place E is ahead: Dx mode equals the deterministic render-complete still, the moving image is navigation.
graft_ideas: Client-side reprojection: carry the render pose P_k in frame metadata and warp the last presented frame to P_now every vsync so motion responds at the platform floor regardless of where pixels come from; the tile viewer should apply the same idea to late tiles and to its 'rendering complete' bookkeeping.

Regulatory framing: Dx mode is the deterministic settled frame only (libjpeg-turbo/PNG pathway, explicit render-complete state), and the moving image is explicitly 'navigation' — the PCoIP build-to-lossless precedent.

Server-side GPU compositing as an optional mode, not the architecture: 40-plex fluorescence, GPU AI overlays and 3D z-stack rendering for thin clients, with SFU fan-out of one render for tumour boards and teaching so N viewers cost one GPU session.
1.25× overscan/oversampled rendering to hide one round trip of pan or ≤1.25× zoom — the streaming analogue of the prefetch ring, useful for any remote-render fallback.

Run the same LOD/prefetch scheduler headless on the server against LAN latencies for still-frame export, thumbnails and Python `Session`-style programmatic rendering (nanobind/PyO3 headless render of the shared core).
An encoder/transport abstraction (NVENC, oneVPL, AMF, SVT-AV1) and a licence blacklist (no x264/x265, no Sunshine/Moonlight linking) if a streaming mode is ever built.
End-to-end tracing by echoing server frame ids from the client, plus a photodiode/high-speed-camera rig from M0 because browsers hide decode and present timing.
